sections.section_name: Section A - Objective Types / MCQs / True-False

questions.question_text: Which component of physical fitness refers to the ability of our muscles to perform exercises continuously over a prolonged duration?
questions.answer: A) Muscular Endurance

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of a warm-up session before participating in vigorous track-and-field athletics?
options: C) To prepare the body and prevent injuries
D) To win the competition immediately
questions.answer: C) To prepare the body and prevent injuries

questions.question_text: In a 100-meter sprint, what is the most important physical quality a runner relies on to finish quickly?
questions.answer: B) Explosive Speed

questions.question_text: True or False: BMI (Body Mass Index) is solely determined by measuring a person's waist circumference.
questions.answer: B) False

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a fundamental motor skill categorized under 'Locomotor movements'?
questions.answer: C) Leaping or running

questions.question_text: What is 'Agility' in the context of motor fitness?
options: A) The ability to lift heavy weights
B) The ability to change body position quickly and accurately
C) The ability to touch your toes
D) The ability to run for an hour without stopping
questions.answer: B) The ability to change body position quickly and accurately

questions.question_text: Which athletics event involves jumping as far as possible horizontally into a sandpit?
questions.answer: B) Long Jump

questions.question_text: True or False: Proper hydration and a balanced diet are critical components of maintaining overall physical well-being.
questions.answer: A) True

questions.question_text: Which test is commonly used to measure the cardiovascular endurance of school students?
questions.answer: A) The 600-meter run/walk test

questions.question_text: What does the 'sit-and-reach' test primarily measure?
options: C) Flexibility of the lower back and hamstrings
questions.answer: C) Flexibility of the lower back and hamstrings

questions.question_text: Define the term 'Motor Fitness' and name one fitness drill used to measure it in school. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Motor fitness is the ability of an individual to perform physical movements efficiently. It includes traits like balance and agility, which can be measured using a shuttle run test.

questions.question_text: What is the main difference between muscular strength and muscular endurance? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Muscular strength is the maximum force a muscle can exert in a single effort, while muscular endurance is the ability to sustain repeated muscle contractions over a long period.

questions.question_text: List any two health benefits of maintaining regular physical activity in daily life. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Regular physical activity strengthens the heart and lungs, improves overall blood circulation, and helps maintain a healthy body weight by burning excess calories.

questions.question_text: Briefly explain the correct technique for holding a baton during a relay race exchange. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Hold the baton securely at its lower end. Extend your arm back steadily so your teammate can firmly grasp the exposed upper section without dropping it during the exchange.

questions.question_text: What is 'reaction time' in athletics, and give one example where it is crucial. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Reaction time is the time taken to respond to a stimulus. It is extremely crucial in a 100-meter sprint when reacting to the starter's gun to gain an early advantage.

questions.question_text: Describe the proper mechanical posture and starting position a runner must maintain during a short-distance sprint start. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The runner must place their feet securely in the starting blocks and bend down with hands spaced shoulder-width apart behind the line. At the 'set' cue, they raise their hips higher than their shoulders, keeping their eyes focused on the track ahead.

questions.question_text: Explain the three main phases of a long jump (approach, takeoff, and landing) and why each is important. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The approach run builds necessary speed. The takeoff requires planting the foot firmly on the board to generate upward lift. A proper two-footed landing in the sandpit prevents injury and ensures maximum horizontal distance is recorded.

questions.question_text: How do you calculate Body Mass Index (BMI), and why is it used in school physical education programs? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: BMI is calculated by dividing a person's weight in kilograms by their height in meters squared. It is used in schools as a simple screening tool to identify potential weight problems and monitor students' overall physical growth and health.

questions.question_text: Detail the physical steps involved in throwing a shot put correctly using the standing throw technique. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Hold the heavy metal ball firmly against the neck under the jaw. Stand sideways in the throwing circle, bend the back knee, and forcefully push the ball forward and upward at an angle, transferring body weight to the front foot.

questions.question_text: A student struggles with breathlessness and fatigue during long-distance running. Recommend a progressive training plan focusing on specific fitness components, and explain how proper warm-up and cool-down routines will improve their performance and recovery over time. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: The student should focus on cardiovascular endurance by starting with brisk walking and gradually progressing to slow jogging. A proper warm-up increases blood flow and prepares the heart, while a cool-down prevents muscle stiffness. Consistent aerobic training will strengthen their lungs, reduce fatigue, and significantly improve their stamina and overall running performance.

questions.question_text: Analyze the mechanics of throwing a javelin. Describe the grip, the approach run, the crossover steps, and the release angle, emphasizing how coordination of different body parts maximizes the distance of the throw. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Grip the javelin securely at the cord. Run forward to build momentum, then transition into crossover steps while leaning back to stretch the throwing muscles. Plant the front foot firmly and forcefully whip the arm forward, releasing the javelin at an optimal 30-40 degree angle. Coordinating the leg drive, torso rotation, and arm swing maximizes the throwing distance.
